TL;DR: 75ms p95 is achievable for 512-token prompts but only with dedicated routing, tuned kernel selection, and tighter admission control. Notes: 

- Baseline: Our hosted median p95 for similar models on dedicated pools is ~60-80ms depending on qps and sequence length. The tail is sensitive to cache misses and bursty simultaneous requests.
- Requirements to guarantee 75ms p95: dedicated capacity (no noisy neighbors), reserved headroom (~20% additional GPUs beyond steady-state), and stricter batching windows to avoid tail amplification.
- Risk: network transit latency and customer-origin throughput variability are outside our control — we should define explicit network carveouts.
- Operational ask: provisioning playbook (SRV-1128) and a 48-hour incident runbook with escalation to SRE on any sustained p95 regression. Also recommend periodic load tests and a 30-day acceptance test after go-live (we can include objectives there).

If sales wants Option B, product will need confirmation on committed GPUs and a staged acceptance plan. I can scope the engineering effort (config + autoscaler knobs) — estimate 3-4 engineering days to produce a validated config and test harness, and an on-call SRE run for acceptance.

Marcus
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
